questions.question: How long can a person remain a minister without being a member of either House of the State Legislature?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**6 months**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• A person can remain a minister without being a member of either House of the State Legislature for a maximum period of **6 months**.
 
• This provision allows an individual to be appointed as a minister and subsequently seek election to either House of the State Legislature within this time frame.
 
• If the individual is not elected within 6 months, they must step down from their ministerial position.
 
• This rule ensures that the executive branch remains accountable to the legislative branch.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• This provision is outlined in **Article 164(4) **of the Constitution of India.
 
• The intent behind this provision is to provide flexibility in the appointment of ministers while ensuring democratic legitimacy through eventual election.
 
• Similar provisions exist for the Union government under **Article 75(5)** of the Constitution.
 
• The Constitution of India aims to balance the need for experienced and capable ministers with the imperative of democratic accountability.

questions.question: Mulk Raj Anand is the author of _____________.

• **Amir Khusrau** is often referred to as 'Tuti-e-Hind', which means 'The Parrot of India'.

• He is also credited with the invention of the tabla and the sitar.

questions.question: The blue green alga Anabaena lives in the leaves of Azolla, a freshwater fern, forming which of the following relationships?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Symbiotic**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Symbiotic** relationships are interactions between two different organisms living in close physical association, typically to the advantage of both.
 
• The blue-green alga **Anabaena** lives in the leaves of the freshwater fern **Azolla**, forming a mutualistic relationship.
 
• In this relationship, **Anabaena** provides nitrogen through nitrogen fixation, which benefits **Azolla**.
 
• **Azolla** provides a habitat and nutrients to **Anabaena**, enabling it to thrive.
 
• This type of relationship is crucial for ecosystems as it enhances the nitrogen content in water bodies, promoting plant growth.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Symbiosis** can be of various types, such as mutualism, commensalism, and parasitism, depending on the nature of the interaction.
 
• The relationship between **Anabaena** and **Azolla** is a classic example of **mutualism**, a type of symbiosis where both partners benefit.
 
• **Anabaena** is known for its ability to fix atmospheric nitrogen, which is a critical nutrient for many plants.
 
• Such symbiotic relationships are also studied for their potential use in sustainable agriculture and water management practices.
 
• Understanding symbiotic relationships helps in the conservation of biodiversity and maintenance of healthy ecosystems.

questions.question: Who was famous for publishing a formula in 1827 that shows the mathematical relationship between current, resistance and voltage?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Georg Simon Ohm**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Georg Simon Ohm** was famous for publishing a formula in 1827 that shows the mathematical relationship between current, resistance, and voltage.
 
• This formula is now known as **Ohm's Law**.
 
• Ohm's Law states that the current flowing through a conductor between two points is directly proportional to the voltage across the two points, provided the temperature remains constant.
 
• The formula is usually written as **V = IR**, where V is the voltage, I is the current, and R is the resistance.
 
• Georg Simon Ohm's work laid the foundation for the field of electrical engineering.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Ohm** was a German physicist and mathematician.
 
• He published his findings in his book titled **"Die galvanische Kette, mathematisch bearbeitet"** (The Galvanic Circuit Investigated Mathematically) in 1827.
 
• Ohm's work was initially met with resistance from the scientific community but later gained recognition for its importance.
 
• In honor of his contributions, the unit of electrical resistance is named the **ohm**, symbolized by Ω.

questions.question: Identify the correct pair (name of shifting agriculture and related state) from the following.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Bewar – Madhya Pradesh**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Bewar** is a traditional form of shifting agriculture practiced in the state of **Madhya Pradesh**.
 
• Shifting agriculture, also known as slash-and-burn agriculture, involves clearing a piece of land by cutting down and burning vegetation, then cultivating crops for a few years before moving to a new area.
 
• This method is often practiced in hilly and forested regions where permanent farming is not feasible.
 
• Other names for shifting agriculture in different regions include **Podu** in Andhra Pradesh and Odisha, **Jhum** in the northeastern states, and **Dahiya** in Rajasthan.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Shifting agriculture is primarily practiced by tribal communities and is an integral part of their cultural heritage.
 
• This agricultural practice is often criticized for its environmental impact, including deforestation and soil erosion, but it also has traditional ecological knowledge and sustainable aspects when practiced in moderation.
 
• Efforts are being made to transition these communities to more sustainable agricultural practices while preserving their cultural identity.

questions.question: The Fundamental Duties of Indian Citizens were adopted from the Constitution of which country?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Soviet Union**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The Fundamental Duties of Indian Citizens were adopted from the Constitution of the **Soviet Union**.
 
• These duties were added to the Indian Constitution by the 42nd Amendment Act, 1976.
 
• They are enumerated in Part IV-A of the Constitution under Article 51A.
 
• There are currently 11 Fundamental Duties listed in the Constitution of India.
 
• The Fundamental Duties serve as a constant reminder to citizens that while enjoying their rights, they also have certain duties to perform towards their country and society.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **The Constitution of India** was adopted by the Constituent Assembly on **26th November 1949 **and **came into effect on 26th January 1950**.
 
• It lays down the framework defining fundamental **political principles, establishes the structure, procedures, powers, and duties of government institutions**, and sets out fundamental rights, directive principles, and the duties of citizens.
 
• The Constitution of India is the **longest written **constitution of any country in the world.
 
• It declares India a **sovereign, socialist, secular, and democratic republic, assuring its citizens justice, equality, and liberty, and endeavors to promote fraternity.**
 
• The **42nd Amendment**, also known as the "Mini-Constitution," brought about several changes, including the addition of the Fundamental Duties.
 
• These duties emphasize the importance of national unity, integrity, and the spirit of common brotherhood amongst all Indians.
 
• The inclusion of Fundamental Duties was intended to bring about a sense of moral obligation among citizens to uphold the spirit of patriotism and to contribute to the nation's well-being.

questions.question: Jet streams are a particular form of:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**geostrophic winds**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Jet streams** are a particular form of geostrophic winds.
 
• These are fast flowing, narrow air currents found in the atmospheres of some planets, including Earth.
 
• Jet streams are typically located near the altitude of the tropopause and are westerly winds (flowing west to east).
 
• They form at the boundaries of adjacent air masses with significant differences in temperature, such as the polar region and the warmer air to the south.
 
• The major jet streams on Earth are the polar jet streams and the subtropical jet streams.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Geostrophic winds** are winds that result from a balance between the Coriolis effect and the pressure gradient force.
 
• These winds flow parallel to the isobars (lines of constant pressure) and are important in the study of meteorology and climate.
 
• Understanding jet streams is crucial for weather forecasting, as they influence weather patterns and the development of storm systems.
 
• Commercial aviation also takes advantage of jet streams to reduce travel time and fuel consumption on certain routes.

questions.question: According to the Global Multidimensional Poverty Index Report 2022, a total of 415 million people exited multidimensional poverty in India in the last ________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**15 years**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **15 years** is the time period during which 415 million people exited multidimensional poverty in India according to the Global Multidimensional Poverty Index Report 2022.
 
• The Global Multidimensional Poverty Index (MPI) is an international measure of acute poverty covering over 100 developing countries.
 
• The MPI identifies multiple deprivations at the household and individual levels in health, education, and standard of living.
 
• India has shown significant progress in reducing multidimensional poverty, reflecting improvements in various socio-economic indicators.
 
• This achievement is crucial for India's overall development and aligns with the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **Global Multidimensional Poverty Index** was developed by the Oxford Poverty and Human Development Initiative (OPHI) and the United Nations Development Programme (UNDP).
 
• The index complements traditional income-based poverty measures by considering multiple factors that contribute to poverty.
 
• India's reduction in multidimensional poverty is attributed to improved access to basic amenities, healthcare, education, and economic opportunities.
 
• The report highlights the importance of sustained policy efforts and targeted interventions to continue this positive trend.
 
• Addressing multidimensional poverty is essential for ensuring inclusive and equitable growth in India.

questions.question: What is the primary function of a commercial bank?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Granting loans and accepting deposits**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The primary function of a commercial bank is **granting loans and accepting deposits**.
 
• Commercial banks play a crucial role in the economy by providing financial services that facilitate business operations and personal financial management.
 
• They accept deposits from individuals and businesses, which can be in the form of savings accounts, checking accounts, and fixed deposits.
 
• These banks also provide loans to individuals and businesses for various purposes, such as purchasing homes, financing businesses, and funding education.
 
• By accepting deposits and providing loans, commercial banks help in the creation of credit, which is essential for economic growth and development.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Commercial banks are different from central banks, which have functions such as issuing currency, conducting monetary policy, and regulating the money supply.
 
• Examples of commercial banks include ICICI Bank, HDFC Bank, and State Bank of India.
 
• Commercial banks are regulated by the country's central banking authority to ensure stability and security in the financial system.
 
• They also offer other financial services such as wealth management, currency exchange, and safe deposit lockers.
 
• Commercial banks generate revenue primarily through the interest charged on loans and the fees for various services they offer.

questions.question: Which of the following is an example of revenue receipt in the government budget?

options.text: Repayment of a loan by a state - owned company
Dividends received from a state - owned enterprise

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Dividends received from a state-owned enterprise**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Dividends received from a state-owned enterprise** are classified as a revenue receipt in the government budget.
 
• Revenue receipts are those receipts that do not lead to a claim on the government. They are non-redeemable and do not create any liabilities.
 
• These include tax revenues like income tax, corporate tax, and non-tax revenues such as dividends and profits from public sector enterprises.
 
• Revenue receipts are crucial for the government as they help in meeting its day-to-day expenditures without increasing its liabilities.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Sale of government-owned land** and **borrowing money from international organizations** are capital receipts as they either create liabilities or reduce assets.
 
• **Repayment of a loan by a state-owned company** is also a capital receipt as it affects the financial assets of the government.
 
• Understanding the distinction between revenue and capital receipts helps in analyzing the financial health and fiscal policies of the government.

questions.question: What was the Swadeshi Movement called in the state of Andhra Pradesh?

questions.question: ‘Midnight’s Children’ is a novel by which of the following writers?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**option 4**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Salman Rushdie** is the author of the novel **'Midnight's Children'**.
 
• The novel was published in **1981** and is considered one of Rushdie's most famous works.
 
• It won the **Booker Prize** in 1981 and the Booker of Bookers in 1993 and 2008, celebrating the best novel among Booker Prize winners.
 
• The story is a loose allegory for events in India both before and after the independence and partition of India.
 
• The protagonist, **Saleem Sinai**, is born at the exact moment when India gains independence, and the novel explores his life intertwined with the history of the nation.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Salman Rushdie** is a British-Indian novelist and essayist.
 
• His work often combines magical realism with historical fiction, primarily concerning the many connections, disruptions, and migrations between Eastern and Western civilizations.
 
• Rushdie's fourth novel, **'The Satanic Verses'**, led to controversies, including a fatwa calling for his assassination issued by Ayatollah Khomeini, the Supreme Leader of Iran, in 1989.
 
• Despite the controversies, Rushdie has continued to write and publish, becoming one of the most influential and celebrated authors in contemporary literature.
